To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the DM capture rate depends on the DM velocity anisotropy and the escape velocity of DM; (ii) the capture rate depends on how the DM halo formed; (iii) the uncertainties on the capture rate are underestimated in the literature; (iv) the capture rate is not a robust quantity to constrain DM properties.
the capture rate is affected by the choice of the DM velocity distribution, but also by the intrinsic variance of that capture rate.

the capture rate by the center of the Sun of DM particles with a mass of 1 TeV is 0.1 times larger if the DM velocity distribution is a Maxwellian distribution than if it is a truncated Maxwellian distribution with a cut-off velocity of 600 km/s, while the corresponding rate is 2 times larger if the velocity distribution is a Gaussian distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the astrophysics of dark matter (DM) and its impact on the capture by the Sun.
the study of the Sun as a dark matter (DM) detector.
the study of the capture of dark matter (DM) by the Sun.

the capture rate is not well controlled, even if it is possible to reduce the uncertainties by considering different velocity distributions.
the DM capture rate uncertainty is not fully controlled by the astrophysical uncertainties.
a WIMP signal coming from the neutrino signal coming the Sun is still a smoking gun, but it would be difficult to interpret it with high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the capture rate of dark matter by the Sun is a very sensitive probe to the local velocity distribution.
the capture rate by the sun is not a well controlled prediction, even if the local DM density is known.
the capture of DM by the center of the Sun is not as robust as it is commonly believed, especially when considering DM particles heavier than a few tens of GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DM capture rate is a very sensitive probe of the DM velocity distribution.
the uncertainties on the capture rate of WIMPs by the Sun are larger than what is usually considered in the literature.
the uncertainties on the local velocity distribution of DM are underestimated and the DM capture rate can vary significantly depending on the velocity distribution.
